output.summary: I believe this is a controlled Mandate 2038 prototype kit, version 0.7.0-rc.3-test, containing the baseline game modules and two defined sessions. Tactics, secret objectives, and Reserve Specialists are explicitly absent. My seat is Mirevanta Works, an imperial research lab with a capability-rusher profile.
observedComponents: Identity and verification materials: kit label, README, rules, manifests, source data, fingerprints, and playtest protocol.

Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and spending 3 Compute. It is global after movement and all requirements are checked when it resolves.

A Facility is Grid-Ready only after receiving complete demand during a completed Production. It reverts if relocated, disconnected from legal Power, or lacking full Power during Production. New, moved, linked, or reconnected Facilities must successfully operate in a later Production before supporting AGI; an Era IV-built Facility cannot support an Era IV declaration.
The first valid AGI declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5. Each declaration adds 3 Scrutiny. Play continues, and victory does not require an AGI declaration.

Fusion requires ending movement on the Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and an available corridor slot. It uses the dedicated marker, occupies one of three Generator slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, adds 3 Scrutiny, counts as an owned Generator for local eligibility and capacity, and does not use the ordinary Generator-piece limit. It cannot be built if the three Grid Generator slots are occupied or the corridor is full.

At the start of each quarter: advance to the next fixed Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award Escalation availability.

Each quarter has three action cycles. Each cycle reveals one Headline into the current Era’s Future Timeline row; players secretly select one Action, reveal simultaneously, resolve clockwise from Initiative as move then act, and pass Initiative clockwise.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. The rival may accept, reject, or issue one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects that counteroffer. No redirecting, renegotiation, or second counteroffer is allowed. Runway, Compute, and Safety may be traded; accepted exchanges happen immediately, promises are non-binding, and a Headline may prohibit a named resource.

If an immediate trade is not accepted, the selected Action continues and is blocked if no legal resolution remains. Immediate trades require no Influence Action; only Influence creates persistent Joint Ventures, lobbying effects, or Trust manipulation.

Discussion and promises create no game state. Formal choices apply only in printed windows; missing responses mean rejection or pass. Paced Play is optional and uses shared sand timers; expiry never creates consent or forces a deal.

Production resolves globally box-by-box for every player: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Within a box, use Initiative order unless specified otherwise; no player completes Production ahead of the others in later boxes without everyone completing the current box first. Apply universal resource caps after every Production gain. [Cross-reference needed: the five Production boxes and their detailed legal-eligibility rules.]

keyRules: Each Era Mandate has a minimum qualification. If nobody qualifies, it scores nothing; otherwise the qualifying leader scores two Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score one each. Compare only the revealed Mandate’s printed criterion; resources, control, and public score do not break ties. Leave scored Mandates beside their Era as public history. The revealed card is authoritative.
Fund: Conservative funding gains 2 Runway; Venture funding gains 4 Runway and 2 Scrutiny. Allocation Exchange provides 1 additional Runway.

Research costs 1 Compute and conducts a Training Run. Capability is provisional until banked. The first card from each ordinary domain adds 1 provisional Capability; after any non-duplicate card, the player may stop and bank or continue. Banking transfers all provisional Capability permanently. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run: lose provisional Capability, add 1 Scrutiny, and end the run. Earlier Scrutiny, Trust, and Runway changes remain; all revealed cards go to discard.

A duplicate may be protected by spending 1 Safety token or by using a Research Commons visit once that run; protection discards the duplicate and immediately banks current provisional Capability. The run cannot continue afterward.

Curated Corpus counts as one not-yet-revealed ordinary domain, or is a duplicate if all are present. Benchmark Leak gives 2 provisional Capability and 1 Scrutiny but is not a domain. Licensed Dataset allows paying 1 Runway to continue, or declining to bank and end. The first Synthetic Loop counts as the unique Loop domain and gives 1 provisional Capability; later copies duplicate. After Loop, the next duplicate cannot be protected. Human Evaluation gives 1 Trust, banks all provisional Capability, and ends the run.
Build has Facility Build and Infrastructure Build. Facility Build constructs a Facility; Infrastructure Build constructs a Generator. Mega-Cluster and Fusion Demonstrator are Escalations.

Constructing a Facility costs 2 Runway, places it on the acting piece’s hex, requires 1 Power during Production, allows only two Facility spaces on non-Frontier hexes, and is never legal on Frontier. Rivals cannot destroy Facilities.

Constructing a Generator requires an Energy hex and is limited to one ordinary Generator per player. Power Corridor costs 1 Runway and creates an Emergency Power Complex; Thermal or Water Basin costs 2 Runway and creates a Civic Heat Battery. Generator construction unlocks in Era II. Each Energy hex has three shared Generator slots. Generators do not use Facility spaces.

Organize can recruit one Team at the acting piece’s destination for 2 Runway and then move one CEO or Team up to two additional adjacent hexes; move CEOs and Teams a combined five adjacent steps; or move one Facility at the destination to an adjacent legal Facility space for 1 Runway. A moved Facility carries starting-grid state, contract halves, and Mega-Cluster host token; recalculate Power eligibility and contract activity, while contract-host identity remains fixed.
Deploy requires 1 Compute and gains 1 Customer, with Capability thresholds of 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 for Customers 1–5. Human Access District waives the Compute cost. Every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny.

Influence moves normally, then permits one effect: at Consensus Network, Civic Permission Authority, or Allocation Exchange, gain 1 Trust or remove 1 Scrutiny, with Consensus Network removing one additional Scrutiny and Civic Permission Authority granting one additional Trust; or at one of your Facilities create or terminate a named Joint Venture with an eligible rival Facility. Political control uses existing CEOs, Teams, and Facilities; Influence creates no separate presence piece.

Two shared ordinary Power Source reference cards define fixed Energy locations. They are never claimed or consumed. Connected ordinary Generators operate automatically during Production. Civic Heat Battery has capacity 3 Power, grants 1 Trust when constructed, and has no recurring penalty. Emergency Power Complex has capacity 4 Power and adds 1 Scrutiny during every Production. Allocation Window: once during Capacity, after a Headline resolves but before Action selection, create 2 temporary Compute. keyRules: Consciousness Efficiency Review: the result lasts for the remainder of the game. Person: Declare AGI requires Trust 4, scores 2 additional Mandate, and removes 1 Scrutiny from the declaring player whenever a declaration resolves. Property: requirements remain normal; each declaration grants the player controlling Civic Permission Authority 2 Runway and adds 1 Systemic Risk cube when it resolves.
The review concerns standing, not subjective experience.

Entanglement Custody: roll Volatility when revealed. On 1–3, Fraud: Fund gains 3 additional Runway and adds 2 additional Scrutiny this cycle. On 4–6, Replicates: Generators provide 2 additional Power this Production. The result is final within the recognized measurement history.
Mandate cards: reveal one from the current Era deck. If nobody meets its minimum qualification, nobody scores. Otherwise, the leader scores 2 Mandate and tied leaders score 1 each.
Capability Becomes Publicly Visible: most Capability gained this Era scores 2 Mandate.
The Demonstration Holds: most unique domains in a player's best successful Training Run scores 2 Mandate.
The Future Attracts Capital: most Runway gained through Fund actions this Era scores 2 Mandate.
The Campus Becomes a Climate: most powered Facilities scores 2 Mandate.
The Future Is Fully Provisioned: most total Power demand satisfied during Production, counting Facilities and Mega-Clusters, scores 2 Mandate; minimum 2.
Compute Becomes a Public Condition: most Compute produced during Production scores 2 Mandate.
The Framework Is Adopted: most new Joint Ventures created this Era that are active during Production scores 2 Mandate; minimum 1.

Public Trust Is Operational: among players who completed a Deploy this Era, most Trust scores 2 Mandate. If none completed Deploy, nobody qualifies by implication of the condition’s eligible group being empty unless another rule says otherwise; confirm in Default Rules if needed [not from this chunk].

output.summary: Mirevanta Works begins with 3 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. The Default Game lasts four Eras, each with three action cycles. Highest final Mandate wins; the shared World Ending is resolved separately.
rulesReconstruction: Setup: build the fixed 13-tile board with Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational districts inside, and six shuffled public districts outside. All CEOs and one Team begin at Frontier; other Teams remain in supply. Give each faction its CEO, three Teams, four Facilities, Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, markers, Scrutiny cubes, and starting resources.

Prepare four Era decks, three Headlines per Era, the Training deck, shared tracks, contract-token pairs, Systemic Risk cubes, Audit bag, Initiative, and Power Source references. The Audit bag begins empty; all Scrutiny cubes begin outside it. Record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of starting Trust values.
Do not use Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, or draft objectives. Begin with Era I and randomly chosen Initiative.

Each Era has three cycles. At the start of the Era, read its New this Era strip, reveal one of three Era Mandates and box the others, ready all six faction Core Actions, and grant that Era's Escalation availability.

Each cycle: reveal the next Headline; resolve any specified before-selection effect; players secretly select one unused Core Action and reveal simultaneously; resolve clockwise from Initiative. Each player moves the acting CEO or Team up to two steps, then resolves the selected Action at the destination. Blocked targets do not cancel movement or exhaustion and give no compensation. Pass Initiative after the cycle.

Core Actions: Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs the Training push-your-luck procedure. Build constructs a Facility or, from Era II, a Generator. Organize recruits, moves personnel, or relocates a Facility for 1 Runway. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains a Customer, subject to Capability thresholds; each Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence can gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or create/terminate an eligible Joint Venture.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer exchanging Runway, Compute, or Safety. Accepted trades occur immediately; promises are non-binding. Counteroffers are limited to one lower counteroffer.

During Production, process all players box-by-box in Initiative order: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Generators operate automatically; Power is assigned to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Facilities produce according to their districts, Customers produce 1 Runway each, and active Mega-Clusters and Joint Ventures produce as specified. Purchased Power costs the buyer 1 Runway per Power paid directly to the supplier, and purchased capacity lasts only that Production.

After Production, a Facility flips Grid-Ready if it received complete demand. A Grid-Ready Facility reverts if relocated, loses legal Power eligibility, or receives insufficient Power. Newly built, moved, linked, or reconnected Facilities require a later successful Production before becoming Grid-Ready again.

End-of-Era Resolution: complete the current cycle's Production and applicable post-Production effects, including Grid-Ready updates, Scrutiny removal, Audit handling, and the Era Mandate scoring procedure. The revealed Mandate scores only if at least one player meets its printed minimum qualification; the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Leave the scored Mandate beside the Era as public history.
After Era IV, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines in Era order. Then lose 1 Mandate per offline Facility, not below zero. Facilities and control provide no separate endgame Mandate.

Resolve the shared World Ending using final AGI declarations, final Collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk cubes in the Audit bag. AGI emerges if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open only if Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count.
World Ending results: AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity.
Highest Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then a joint victory with the stated merger announcement.

output.summary: Default Game is a four-Era, four-player-style institutional competition. Corthaven begins as the foundry faction with CEO Eli Rosen, 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Each Era has three simultaneous action cycles, followed by Audit and Era transition procedures. The highest final Mandate wins; the World Ending is resolved separately.
rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed thirteen-hex board: Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles in the outer ring. Frontier has no Facility spaces; every other hex has two Facility spaces, a visit bonus, production, and a control value.

Place all CEOs and one Team per faction at Frontier; the other two Teams remain in supply. Use each faction’s printed starting tracks and already-earned public Mandate. Corthaven’s recorded starting state is 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 Mandate.

Give each faction its CEO, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI Declaration card, markers, and ten Scrutiny cubes. Scrutiny begins outside the Audit bag; the bag is initially empty. The first Facility carries the integrated starting-grid identifier, but its exact identity and placement procedure are not recorded.

Prepare the Default-eligible Headlines by Era, excluding Advanced Play cards. Each Era has three Headlines; reveal one per action cycle into that Era’s Future Timeline row. Prepare four three-card Era Mandate decks and the Training deck.

Begin Era I, Progress. At Era start, ready all six Core Actions, grant the Era’s Escalation availability, reveal one Mandate card and box the other two unseen, and read the Era’s New this Era strip. Era I grants no Escalation availability and has Audit base 2.

Each Era contains three action cycles. At the start of each cycle, reveal a Headline. Players secretly select one unused Core Action or spend one available Escalation for an unlocked Escalation, then reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative.

For each selected Action, move one CEO or Team zero to two adjacent hexes, then resolve the Action at the destination. Apply effects in precedence order: Era global unlocks, faction-board modification, current Headline effect, ordinary Action plus at most one destination bonus, faction modifier, and applicable global effects. Exhaust the Core Action or flip the Escalation after resolution, then pass Initiative clockwise.

If another player consumes a legal target before a later player resolves, the later player still moves and exhausts the Action but gets no effect or compensation. If an Action becomes blocked after reveal, retain the selection and choose any legal piece, movement, mode, target, payment, and immediate trade.

Corthaven’s Core Actions are: Fund for 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny; Research for 1 Compute and a push-your-luck Training Run; Build for a Facility or Generator; Organize for recruitment, Team redistribution, or Facility relocation; Deploy for 1 Compute to gain a Customer if permitted; and Influence for Trust, Scrutiny removal, or negotiation from a Facility.

Runway is capped at 12, Compute at 10, and Safety at 3 after gains or trades. Capability is permanent and spent only when instructed. Mandate awards are public, immediate, and permanent; later losses of Customers, Capability, or Trust do not remove threshold awards.

During Capacity, Corthaven may use Allocation Window once after a Headline resolves and before Action selection: create two temporary Compute and offer each token separately to a rival for a Runway price no greater than that rival’s current Runway. The rival may reject or make one lower counterprice; Corthaven accepts or rejects. No further negotiation is allowed; untraded temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

Corthaven’s Shovels ability triggers when another player spends at least 2 Compute in one Action, granting Corthaven 1 Runway, at most twice per Era. The exact definition of qualifying Compute expenditure is unresolved.
Era II is Capacity: ready all Core Actions, grant one Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 3. It unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization.

Era III is Authority: ready all Core Actions, grant one Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 4. It unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Narrative Capture is global after movement: remove two personal Scrutiny, gain two Runway, or give one Scrutiny to a player with more Customers.

Era IV is Continuity: ready all Core Actions, grant two Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 5. It unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Agent Swarm spends one Era IV Escalation availability and two different unused Core Actions. Move once, resolve both Actions from the destination in either order, apply the visit bonus to only one, exhaust both Actions, flip Agent Swarm, and add three Scrutiny.

Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. Requirements are checked when it resolves. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5; every declaration adds 3 Scrutiny. The Person variant additionally requires Trust 4, scores 2 Mandate, and removes 1 Scrutiny; the Property variant gives the Civic Permission Authority controller 2 Runway and adds 1 Systemic Risk cube. The selection of variant is not recorded.

Fusion requires ending movement at the Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and constructing Fusion there. It occupies one of three Generator slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. It cannot be built if the slots or Corridor are full.

Power is local. The starting grid powers only its assigned first Facility. Each Generator powers Facilities on its own or an adjacent hex; Facilities cannot relay Power. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after receiving complete demand during completed Production, and loses Grid-Ready status if relocated, disconnected, or underpowered.

At each action cycle, immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged. The rival may accept, reject, or make one complete counteroffer; no counter-counteroffer, redirection, renegotiation, or binding future promise is allowed. Accepted trades transfer immediately; Influence is required for persistent Joint Ventures, lobbying, or Trust manipulation. Negotiation creates no state unless accepted under these rules, and the exact blocked-trade condition follows the formal window rules not included here.

rulesReconstruction: Setup: Build the thirteen-tile board with Frontier central, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles in the outer ring. The tiles are Frontier; two Research Commons; two Compute Estates; Human Access District; Fabrication Corridor; Allocation Exchange; Workforce Transition District; Consensus Network; Civic Permission Authority; Power Corridor; and Thermal and Water Basin.

Separate Headlines by Era, exclude Advanced Play cards, and reserve a twelve-card Future Timeline with three rows of three cards per Era. Divide the twelve Era Mandate cards into four three-card Era decks. Shuffle Training. Place shared tracks and supplies, including Audit, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Fusion, Initiative, and Power Source references.

Each player receives their faction board, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, Generator, Customer and Escalation markers, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, and other listed components. All CEOs, Teams, and Facilities begin at Frontier unless the component/setup reference says otherwise; Frontier cannot be controlled and has no Facility spaces, production, or contract icon.

Loopfold AI begins with Mateo Ibarra, 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate. Its Platform sequence begins at 1 Customer; its next Deploy requires 4 Capability. Its first Deploy each Era on Human Access District or Consensus Network costs 0 Compute. Its Social Graph may use a controlled Human Access District or Consensus Network as a remote Deploy destination, including that tile’s visit bonus and destination-dependent effects.

Set Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, and Safety from each faction board. Place each faction’s printed starting public Mandate once on the shared track and record total Setup Collective Trust for the final World Ending comparison. Put all Scrutiny cubes outside the Audit bag; the exact initial bag contents remain unspecified. Choose Initiative and begin Era I, Progress.

Each Era has three action cycles. At each cycle start, reveal one Headline into that Era’s Future Timeline row, resolve its printed effect and duration, then players secretly select one available Core Action and reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: move up to two steps, then act. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

A normal Action is selected before movement and cannot be replaced after reveal. If a later player’s legal target is consumed earlier, the later Action still moves and exhausts with no effect or compensation. If an Action has no legal resolution, the precise blocked-action fallback remains unresolved.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny for Venture funding; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training, with provisional Capability banked or lost according to duplicate, protection, Licensed Dataset, Synthetic Loop, and Human Evaluation rules. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits or moves pieces or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute normally, requires 2/4/6/8/10 Capability for Customers 1–5, gains one Customer, and adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence can gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or create/terminate a Joint Venture from a Facility.

Movement crosses shared tile edges; CEOs and Teams may move zero, one, or two steps. Rival pieces coexist and there is no combat. Presence is CEO 2, Team 1, Facility 1; highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex, with tied highest presence meaning no control. District visit bonuses apply at the destination. Frontier may optionally provide 1 Runway and 1 Scrutiny after Act.

Facilities cost 2 Runway, cannot be built on Frontier, occupy Facility spaces, and require complete demand and legal Power during Production. Generators unlock in Capacity; each player may construct one ordinary Generator on an Energy hex, subject to shared three-slot limits. Power Corridor construction costs 1 Runway and gives 4 Power plus recurring Scrutiny; Thermal and Water Basin costs 2 Runway and gives 3 Power plus 1 Trust when built. Local Power is recalculated after movement or connection changes.

Negotiation permits one complete resource offer to one rival immediately before or after Act. The rival may accept, reject, or publish one complete counteroffer, which the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be traded, subject to Headline restrictions; accepted trades occur immediately and future promises are non-binding.

At the end of the Era, resolve the quarter sequence: advance to the next fixed Era, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and box the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. The exact placement of Audit, Production, Mandate scoring, and next-quarter transition within End-of-Era Resolution is not fully established by the notes.

Production is synchronized. Customers produce Runway: Customers 1–3 produce 2 each for public Mandate purposes, while Customers 4–5 produce 1 each and increase public exposure. Powered Facilities and other Power-dependent systems resolve their printed production. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after complete demand is satisfied in a completed Production allocation; it becomes unready after relocation, loss of legal Power, or insufficient Production Power.

Audit and Systemic Risk resolve using the Era Audit base, Scrutiny cubes in the opaque bag, and any black Systemic Risk cubes. Exact draw, placement, penalty, and timing details are not fully present in the notes. Scrutiny removal returns that faction’s cubes from the bag to its supply, removing as many as possible.

Era Mandate scoring uses the revealed card’s printed minimum qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Resources, control, and public score do not break Mandate ties. Scored Mandates remain as public history. Starting public Mandate is never scored again.

Era progression is Progress, Capacity, Authority, Continuity. Progress unlocks the starting grid, Training, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Capacity unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Authority unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Continuity unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Escalation availability is 0, 1, 1, and 2 respectively, with earlier unused Escalations retained from Authority onward.

In Continuity, Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute, unless a Headline modifies the threshold. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5; each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and an open Generator slot; it provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Final resolution: read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud by Era. Each offline Facility costs its owner 1 Mandate, never reducing that player below zero. Facilities, control, and stored resources provide no separate final Mandate. Determine the shared World Ending from AGI declarations, final Collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk. AGI exists if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count.

The World Ending is The Singularity for AGI plus Open, The Closed Loop for AGI plus Closed, The Plural Future for no AGI plus Open, and Assured Continuity for no AGI plus Closed. Read the selected narrative, then highest Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.

output.summary: Default Game, four Eras, for 3–5 players. As Kestralyn (Jiwon Park), begin with 6 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Use the fixed modular 13-tile board, three Era Headlines and one revealed Era Mandate per Era, three action cycles per Era, and Default rules only. Kestralyn discounts its first Facility Build each Era by 1 Runway and scores 1 Mandate when that discount actually reduces the cost of a completed Facility. Its once-per-game Orbital Compute may relocate one Facility to any legal open Facility space during movement, carrying attachments and designations; recalculate Power eligibility, resolve production immediately if currently available capacity can power it, then add 2 Scrutiny.
rulesReconstruction: Setup: Build Frontier at the center, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. Place shared tracks, supplies, Audit bag, Initiative marker, Power references, and all faction components. Every CEO and one Team begin at Frontier; other Teams remain in supply. Set faction tracks to printed starts, place Kestralyn’s 2 public Mandate, and record printed starting Trust totals as Setup Collective Trust. Place all Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag. Choose Initiative randomly and begin Era I.

Each Era: Use its Era card, three eligible Default Headlines, and its three-card Era Mandate deck. At the start of the Era/quarter, advance to the Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era’s Escalation availability. Era I has Audit base 2; Era II 3; Era III 4; Era IV 5. The Era cards progressively unlock Training, starting-grid Facilities, Customers, Scrutiny, Generators, Mega-Cluster, Reorganization, agreements, Open Weights, Narrative Capture, signature programs, Agent Swarm, AGI, and Fusion.

Action cycle: Reveal one Headline before secret selection. Players simultaneously select one unused Core Action or unlocked Escalation, reveal, then resolve clockwise from Initiative. Each player moves its acting CEO/Team zero to two adjacent steps, or uses the selected effect’s movement, then resolves the Action from the destination. Pass Initiative clockwise afterward. Played Core Actions remain exhausted until the next Era; blocked Actions still exhaust after movement and give no compensation. No rewind occurs.

Core Actions: Fund gains 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway with 2 Scrutiny; Venture funding is the latter. Research spends 1 Compute for a Training Run, with provisional Capability banked on stopping, duplicate crashes unless protected, and special Training cards following their printed effects. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits, redistributes Teams, or relocates a Facility. Deploy spends 1 Compute and requires the next Capability threshold (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), unless Human Access District waives the cost; each Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence changes Trust/Scrutiny at named locations or creates/terminates a Joint Venture. Kestralyn’s first Facility Build each Era receives its 1-Runway discount.

Trading and negotiation: Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer to one rival involving Runway, Compute, or Safety. The rival accepts, rejects, or makes one complete counteroffer; the original player accepts or rejects. No further negotiation is allowed, and promises are non-binding. Influence is required for persistent Joint Ventures, lobbying, or Trust manipulation; immediate trades do not require Influence.

Production: Resolve globally and box-by-box in Initiative order: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner. All players finish the current box before anyone proceeds to the next. Assign legal local Power, generate resources, trade/allocate as permitted, produce from powered Facilities and other sources, and resolve partnerships. Apply resource caps immediately: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless Kestralyn’s board changes them. Facilities become Grid-Ready only after complete demand is met during completed Production; relocation, disconnection, or insufficient Power flips them back.

End-of-Era Resolution: The notes establish the quarter/Production sequence and Era Mandate reveal, but do not provide a complete, authoritative End-of-Era procedure. At minimum, resolve the Era’s remaining Production/Audit effects, apply Scrutiny and Systemic Risk handling, preserve the revealed Headline in the Future Timeline, and carry forward only rules explicitly marked persistent or unused Escalation availability. The exact timing of Audit, Mandate scoring, and reset/cleanup must be confirmed before play.

Scoring: Score Mandates immediately when their conditions resolve. Customer thresholds, Capability thresholds (3/6/9/12), Trust thresholds (2/4/6), printed Headlines, Era Mandates, Fusion, faction abilities, and AGI can award Mandate. An Era Mandate scores only if its minimum qualification is met: the qualifying leader gets 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders get 1 each. Use only the revealed card’s printed criterion. Facilities, control, stored resources, and unused cards do not otherwise score.

Era IV systems: Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, resolves both from one destination in either order, exhausts both, flips the component, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires the Power Corridor, 5 Runway, and an available corridor slot; it provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, adds 3 Scrutiny, and occupies a Fusion slot.

Ending: Read the 12-card Future Timeline aloud by Era. Apply −1 Mandate for each offline Facility, floored at zero. Resolve the shared World Ending using whether any institution ends with AGI and Capability at least 9, final Collective Trust versus Setup Collective Trust plus player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk cubes in the Audit bag. AGI plus Open gives The Singularity; AGI plus Closed gives The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open gives The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed gives Assured Continuity. Then announce the institution with the highest final Mandate after reading its claimed history. Ties break by Trust, then Customers, then Compute, then joint victory with a merger announcement. There is no other endgame scoring; Advanced Play and secret objectives are excluded.

output.summary: Default Game is a four-Era, four-player-style institutional competition. Corthaven begins as the foundry faction with CEO Eli Rosen, 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Each Era has three simultaneous action cycles, followed by Audit and Era transition procedures. The highest final Mandate wins; the World Ending is resolved separately.
rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed thirteen-hex board: Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles in the outer ring. Frontier has no Facility spaces; every other hex has two Facility spaces, a visit bonus, production, and a control value.

Place all CEOs and one Team per faction at Frontier; the other two Teams remain in supply. Use each faction’s printed starting tracks and already-earned public Mandate. Corthaven’s recorded starting state is 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 Mandate.

Give each faction its CEO, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI Declaration card, markers, and ten Scrutiny cubes. Scrutiny begins outside the Audit bag; the bag is initially empty. The first Facility carries the integrated starting-grid identifier, but its exact identity and placement procedure are not recorded.

Prepare the Default-eligible Headlines by Era, excluding Advanced Play cards. Each Era has three Headlines; reveal one per action cycle into that Era’s Future Timeline row. Prepare four three-card Era Mandate decks and the Training deck.

Begin Era I, Progress. At Era start, ready all six Core Actions, grant the Era’s Escalation availability, reveal one Mandate card and box the other two unseen, and read the Era’s New this Era strip. Era I grants no Escalation availability and has Audit base 2.

Each Era contains three action cycles. At the start of each cycle, reveal a Headline. Players secretly select one unused Core Action or spend one available Escalation for an unlocked Escalation, then reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative.

For each selected Action, move one CEO or Team zero to two adjacent hexes, then resolve the Action at the destination. Apply effects in precedence order: Era global unlocks, faction-board modification, current Headline effect, ordinary Action plus at most one destination bonus, faction modifier, and applicable global effects. Exhaust the Core Action or flip the Escalation after resolution, then pass Initiative clockwise.

If another player consumes a legal target before a later player resolves, the later player still moves and exhausts the Action but gets no effect or compensation. If an Action becomes blocked after reveal, retain the selection and choose any legal piece, movement, mode, target, payment, and immediate trade.

Corthaven’s Core Actions are: Fund for 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny; Research for 1 Compute and a push-your-luck Training Run; Build for a Facility or Generator; Organize for recruitment, Team redistribution, or Facility relocation; Deploy for 1 Compute to gain a Customer if permitted; and Influence for Trust, Scrutiny removal, or negotiation from a Facility.

Runway is capped at 12, Compute at 10, and Safety at 3 after gains or trades. Capability is permanent and spent only when instructed. Mandate awards are public, immediate, and permanent; later losses of Customers, Capability, or Trust do not remove threshold awards.

During Capacity, Corthaven may use Allocation Window once after a Headline resolves and before Action selection: create two temporary Compute and offer each token separately to a rival for a Runway price no greater than that rival’s current Runway. The rival may reject or make one lower counterprice; Corthaven accepts or rejects. No further negotiation is allowed; untraded temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

Corthaven’s Shovels ability triggers when another player spends at least 2 Compute in one Action, granting Corthaven 1 Runway, at most twice per Era. The exact definition of qualifying Compute expenditure is unresolved.
Era II is Capacity: ready all Core Actions, grant one Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 3. It unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization.

Era III is Authority: ready all Core Actions, grant one Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 4. It unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Narrative Capture is global after movement: remove two personal Scrutiny, gain two Runway, or give one Scrutiny to a player with more Customers.

Era IV is Continuity: ready all Core Actions, grant two Escalation availability, play three cycles, and use Audit base 5. It unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Agent Swarm spends one Era IV Escalation availability and two different unused Core Actions. Move once, resolve both Actions from the destination in either order, apply the visit bonus to only one, exhaust both Actions, flip Agent Swarm, and add three Scrutiny.

Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. Requirements are checked when it resolves. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5; every declaration adds 3 Scrutiny. The Person variant additionally requires Trust 4, scores 2 Mandate, and removes 1 Scrutiny; the Property variant gives the Civic Permission Authority controller 2 Runway and adds 1 Systemic Risk cube. The selection of variant is not recorded.

Fusion requires ending movement at the Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and constructing Fusion there. It occupies one of three Generator slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. It cannot be built if the slots or Corridor are full.

Power is local. The starting grid powers only its assigned first Facility. Each Generator powers Facilities on its own or an adjacent hex; Facilities cannot relay Power. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after receiving complete demand during completed Production, and loses Grid-Ready status if relocated, disconnected, or underpowered.

At each action cycle, immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged. The rival may accept, reject, or make one complete counteroffer; no counter-counteroffer, redirection, renegotiation, or binding future promise is allowed. Accepted trades transfer immediately; Influence is required for persistent Joint Ventures, lobbying, or Trust manipulation. Negotiation creates no state unless accepted under these rules, and the exact blocked-trade condition follows the formal window rules not included here.

Seat 4 is Loopfold AI, beginning at Frontier with Mateo Ibarra, 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 already-earned public Mandate. rulesReconstruction: Setup: Build the thirteen-tile board with Frontier central, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles in the outer ring. The tiles are Frontier; two Research Commons; two Compute Estates; Human Access District; Fabrication Corridor; Allocation Exchange; Workforce Transition District; Consensus Network; Civic Permission Authority; Power Corridor; and Thermal and Water Basin.

Separate Headlines by Era, exclude Advanced Play cards, and reserve a twelve-card Future Timeline with three rows of three cards per Era. Divide the twelve Era Mandate cards into four three-card Era decks. Shuffle Training. Place shared tracks and supplies, including Audit, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Fusion, Initiative, and Power Source references.

Each player receives their faction board, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, Generator, Customer and Escalation markers, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, and other listed components. All CEOs, Teams, and Facilities begin at Frontier unless the component/setup reference says otherwise; Frontier cannot be controlled and has no Facility spaces, production, or contract icon.

Loopfold AI begins with Mateo Ibarra, 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate. Its Platform sequence begins at 1 Customer; its next Deploy requires 4 Capability. Its first Deploy each Era on Human Access District or Consensus Network costs 0 Compute. Its Social Graph may use a controlled Human Access District or Consensus Network as a remote Deploy destination, including that tile’s visit bonus and destination-dependent effects.

Set Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, and Safety from each faction board. Place each faction’s printed starting public Mandate once on the shared track and record total Setup Collective Trust for the final World Ending comparison. Put all Scrutiny cubes outside the Audit bag; the exact initial bag contents remain unspecified. Choose Initiative and begin Era I, Progress.

Each Era has three action cycles. At each cycle start, reveal one Headline into that Era’s Future Timeline row, resolve its printed effect and duration, then players secretly select one available Core Action and reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: move up to two steps, then act. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

A normal Action is selected before movement and cannot be replaced after reveal. If a later player’s legal target is consumed earlier, the later Action still moves and exhausts with no effect or compensation. If an Action has no legal resolution, the precise blocked-action fallback remains unresolved.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny for Venture funding; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training, with provisional Capability banked or lost according to duplicate, protection, Licensed Dataset, Synthetic Loop, and Human Evaluation rules. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits or moves pieces or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute normally, requires 2/4/6/8/10 Capability for Customers 1–5, gains one Customer, and adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence can gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or create/terminate a Joint Venture from a Facility.

Movement crosses shared tile edges; CEOs and Teams may move zero, one, or two steps. Rival pieces coexist and there is no combat. Presence is CEO 2, Team 1, Facility 1; highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex, with tied highest presence meaning no control. District visit bonuses apply at the destination. Frontier may optionally provide 1 Runway and 1 Scrutiny after Act.

Facilities cost 2 Runway, cannot be built on Frontier, occupy Facility spaces, and require complete demand and legal Power during Production. Generators unlock in Capacity; each player may construct one ordinary Generator on an Energy hex, subject to shared three-slot limits. Power Corridor construction costs 1 Runway and gives 4 Power plus recurring Scrutiny; Thermal and Water Basin costs 2 Runway and gives 3 Power plus 1 Trust when built. Local Power is recalculated after movement or connection changes.

Negotiation permits one complete resource offer to one rival immediately before or after Act. The rival may accept, reject, or publish one complete counteroffer, which the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be traded, subject to Headline restrictions; accepted trades occur immediately and future promises are non-binding.

At the end of the Era, resolve the quarter sequence: advance to the next fixed Era, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and box the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. The exact placement of Audit, Production, Mandate scoring, and next-quarter transition within End-of-Era Resolution is not fully established by the notes.

Production is synchronized. Customers produce Runway: Customers 1–3 produce 2 each for public Mandate purposes, while Customers 4–5 produce 1 each and increase public exposure. Powered Facilities and other Power-dependent systems resolve their printed production. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after complete demand is satisfied in a completed Production allocation; it becomes unready after relocation, loss of legal Power, or insufficient Production Power.

Audit and Systemic Risk resolve using the Era Audit base, Scrutiny cubes in the opaque bag, and any black Systemic Risk cubes. Exact draw, placement, penalty, and timing details are not fully present in the notes. Scrutiny removal returns that faction’s cubes from the bag to its supply, removing as many as possible.

Era Mandate scoring uses the revealed card’s printed minimum qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Resources, control, and public score do not break Mandate ties. Scored Mandates remain as public history. Starting public Mandate is never scored again.

Era progression is Progress, Capacity, Authority, Continuity. Progress unlocks the starting grid, Training, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Capacity unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Authority unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Continuity unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Escalation availability is 0, 1, 1, and 2 respectively, with earlier unused Escalations retained from Authority onward.

In Continuity, Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute, unless a Headline modifies the threshold. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5; each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and an open Generator slot; it provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Final resolution: read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud by Era. Each offline Facility costs its owner 1 Mandate, never reducing that player below zero. Facilities, control, and stored resources provide no separate final Mandate. Determine the shared World Ending from AGI declarations, final Collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk. AGI exists if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count.

The World Ending is The Singularity for AGI plus Open, The Closed Loop for AGI plus Closed, The Plural Future for no AGI plus Open, and Assured Continuity for no AGI plus Closed. Read the selected narrative, then highest Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.

Mega-Clusters add two additional Power demand; solo projects require both hosts plus that demand, while joint projects require each participant’s host plus one additional demand.
findings.heading: Power delivery ◆

findings.evidence: The local-Power test is same-hex or adjacent-hex connectivity from a Generator to a Facility. The starting grid powers only its assigned first Facility; Facilities cannot relay Power to other Facilities. Eligibility must be recalculated whenever a Facility or Generator moves.
findings.heading: Power connections ◆

findings.evidence: Era IV grants each player two Escalation availability. Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both from that destination in either order, pays all costs, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, flips Agent Swarm, and adds three Scrutiny. Fusion Demonstrator requires ending movement on the Power Corridor and spending five Runway; it occupies one of three Generator slots, provides six Power, scores two Mandate, adds three Scrutiny, counts as an owned Generator for local Power eligibility and capacity, and cannot be built if all three slots are occupied or the corridor is full. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, three Customers, three Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and three Compute; it adds three Scrutiny. A Facility is Grid-Ready only after receiving complete demand during completed Production; it flips back if relocated, disconnected, or underpowered in Production. Era-IV-built Facilities cannot support a declaration that Era.
findings.heading: Era IV — Continuity

findings.evidence: Declare AGI checks all requirements when it resolves. The first valid declaration scores seven Mandate; later declarations score five. Every declaration adds three Scrutiny.
findings.heading: Declare AGI

findings.evidence: During Allocate, starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power may be allocated only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Purchased Power lasts only for that Production; starting-grid and emergency Power cannot be sold. A supplier may sell at most one Power, and only installed Generator or Fusion capacity may be sold.
findings.heading: C. Power and Production

findings.evidence: The ordinary quarter sequence is: begin the quarter and reveal the Era/Mandate; run three action cycles; resolve Power and Production; conduct Public Audit; then score the Mandate. Production is completed in synchronized boxes for all players: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner.
findings.heading: 6. Era sequence

findings.evidence: Public Audit draws two, three, four, or five cubes in a four-player game for Eras I–IV, respectively, with player-count-adjusted profiles provided for two through six players. Colored cubes in Eras I–III cost the owner one Runway or one Trust. In Era IV they cost two Runway or one Mandate, with specified fallback rules. Drawn colored cubes return to supply; undrawn cubes remain in the bag. A drawn black Systemic Risk cube gives every player with at least three Customers the current Era penalty, then returns to supply; black cubes left at game end are unresolved Systemic Risk.
findings.heading: D. Public Audit

findings.evidence: Power Production proceeds through Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, and Partner. Allocate combines starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power and assigns it only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Fusion occupies one of the Power Corridor tile’s three Generator slots, provides six Power, and counts as an owned Generator for local eligibility and capacity.
findings.heading: C. Power and Production

findings.evidence: The Audit bag is opaque. Public Audit draws the Era/player-count profile amount or stops when empty. Colored cubes in Eras I–III impose one Runway or one Trust; Era IV imposes two Runway or one Mandate. Drawn colored cubes return to supply, undrawn cubes remain in the bag. Black Systemic Risk affects every player with at least three Customers and returns to supply when drawn; black cubes remaining at game end are unresolved.
findings.heading: D. Public Audit

findings.evidence: The source orders the ordinary Era/quarter process as: Begin the quarter, three action cycles, synchronized Power and Production, Public Audit, then Mandate scoring. Production boxes are resolved for every player before advancing to the next box.
findings.heading: 6. Era sequence

findings.evidence: Mandate scoring: each Era Mandate has a minimum qualification; if nobody qualifies, it scores for nobody. Otherwise, the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Compare only the revealed card’s printed criterion; resources, control, and public score do not break ties. Leave the scored card beside its Era. Headline is revealed before secret action selection, resolved for its printed effect/duration, and left face up in the Era row; its rules normally expire at the end of the current cycle unless it names that Era’s Production.
findings.heading: 6. Era sequence

findings.evidence: Research duplicates normally crash the run: lose all provisional Capability, add 1 Scrutiny, and end the run. Spending 1 Safety, or using a Research Commons visit once during that run, discards the duplicate and immediately banks current provisional Capability; the run cannot continue. Scrutiny, Trust, and Runway changes before a crash are not reversed.
findings.heading: Research

findings.evidence: Capability earned during Research is provisional until banked. Banking adds all provisional Capability to permanent Capability. Human Evaluation immediately banks all provisional Capability and ends the run. An unprotected duplicate loses all provisional Capability.
findings.heading: Research

findings.evidence: The revealed Mandate card is the exact qualification and scoring authority. Each Mandate has a minimum qualification; a qualifying sole leader scores 2 Mandate, while tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Only the printed criterion is compared, and the scored card remains beside its Era.
findings.heading: 9. Printed card authorities

findings.evidence: Constructing an ordinary Generator requires the acting piece to be on an Energy hex; each player may construct one ordinary Generator, and each Energy hex has three shared Generator slots. Power Corridor constructs an Emergency Power Complex for 1 Runway; Thermal or Water Basin constructs a Civic Heat Battery for 2 Runway. Connected ordinary Generators operate automatically during Production. Fusion Demonstrator is an Era IV Escalation.
findings.heading: Build ◆

findings.evidence: Headlines are revealed before secret action selection, resolved according to their printed effect and duration, and left face up in the Era row. Three Headlines per Era form the twelve-card Future Timeline. Unless a Headline names the current Era’s Production, its rules expire at the end of the current cycle. At game end, earned Mandate already on the public track is not scored again.
findings.heading: 9. Printed card authorities

findings.evidence: Final scoring sequence: read the twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud Era by Era; lose one Mandate per offline Facility; resolve the shared World Ending; announce the highest-Mandate institution only after reading the history it claims to have won. Offline penalties cannot reduce Mandate below zero.
findings.heading: 11. Final scoring

findings.evidence: At final scoring, each offline Facility costs one Mandate. This penalty cannot reduce a player below zero Mandate. The chunk does not define complete Facility demand or the offline test.
findings.heading: 11. Final scoring

findings.evidence: AGI emerges only if at least one declaring institution finishes the game at Capability 9 or higher; a declaration that finishes below Capability 9 does not qualify. A qualified declaration alone does not make the ending Open.

findings.evidence: The final-scoring order is Headlines, offline-Facility Mandate losses, shared World Ending resolution, then announcement of the highest-Mandate institution after its claimed history is read. No complete Era-end sequence is provided here.

findings.evidence: Corthaven’s printed faction abilities are The Shovels — Demand-Linked Supply and Allocation Window — Priority Allocation Window. The Shovels triggers when another player spends at least 2 Compute in one action, granting Corthaven 1 Runway, at most twice per Era. Allocation Window is usable once during Capacity, after Headline resolution and before Action selection; it creates 2 temporary Compute, each offered to a rival for a Runway price, with one counterprice allowed. Temporary Compute disappears at cycle end. No other Corthaven signature or Era IV faction ability is listed in this source chunk.

findings.evidence: Mandate resolution: reveal one card from the current Era deck; if nobody meets its minimum qualification, nobody scores; otherwise the leader scores 2 Mandate and tied leaders score 1 each.
